ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two JK flip-flops in the figure, the left one is FF1 and the right one is FF2; the FF1 output is labeled Q1, and the FF2 output is labeled Q2. The J and K terminals of both flip-flops are both in the toggle operating mode of logic 1. FF1 is triggered by the external clock CP, and FF2 is cascade-triggered by the transition of the previous-stage Q1, so it is necessary to see whether the transition of Q1 is the effective triggering edge of FF2. Reasoning: The initial state Q2Q1=00. Because FF1 toggles when each CP pulse arrives, Q1 toggles once per pulse. According to the cascade triggering relationship in the figure, FF2 toggles only when Q1 has its effective triggering transition; within 4 CP pulses, Q1 experiences 0→1, 1→0, 0→1, 1→0, and there are two effective triggering transitions causing Q2 to toggle. Therefore the state changes can be listed as: initial state 00; after the 1st pulse Q1 toggles and Q2 remains unchanged, giving 01; after the 2nd pulse Q1 toggles back to 0 and Q2 toggles, giving 10; after the 3rd pulse Q1 toggles and Q2 remains unchanged, giving 11; after the 4th pulse Q1 toggles back to 0 and Q2 toggles again, giving 00. Thus after 4 clock pulses Q2Q1 returns to 00.

On each clock pulse, toggle Q1. Then check whether the transition of Q1 is the active triggering transition for FF2 and toggle Q2 accordingly. Over four CP pulses, Q1 toggles four times and returns to 0, while Q2 toggles twice and also returns to 0. Therefore the final state Q2Q1 is 00.
